name: Double Draw (Lowball)
description: Double Draw (specifically Double Draw Lowball) is a poker variant that expands the traditional Draw Poker format by adding a second opportunity for players to improve their hands. While most commonly played as a 'Lowball' game (where the lowest hand wins), it can also be played for high hands. The extra draw phase significantly increases the chances of completing complex hands but also requires deeper bankroll management and bluffing skills.

history.origins: Double Draw rose to prominence in the midnd20th century in California card rooms (like Gardena) as a way to increase action and pot sizes in standard Lowball games.
timeline: 1930s-40s: Lowball becomes the preferred game in legal California card rooms.
1970s: Double Draw variants are introduced to attract more recreational players to the tables.
Modern Era: Occasionally featured in 'Dealer's Choice' games and specific online poker 'Mixed Game' rotations.
history.cultural: Known for its highndvariance gameplay, it is often called a 'gambler's variant' of traditional poker.
history.evolution: The addition of the second draw was a direct response to the 'mechanical' nature of singlenddraw games, where hand strength is often too obvious after the first draw.

setup.players: 2 to 6 players. Usually played with Blinds (Small and Big).
setup.equipment: Poker chips, dealer button, standard deck.

rules.objective: Complete the lowest possible 5-card hand (Lowball) or highest possible (High) after two drawing rounds.
rules.gameplay:
1. Opening: First betting round occurs after the initial 5 cards are dealt.
2. First Draw: Players may discard any number of cards and receive new ones from the dealer.
3. Second Betting: A second round of betting takes place.
4. Second Draw: Players may discard and draw a second time.
5. Final Betting: The final round of betting occurs before the showdown.
keyRules: Players are not required to discard; they can 'stand pat' on either draw.
If the deck runs out of cards during a draw, the discarded cards (excluding the current player's discards) are reshuffled to create a new deck.
The bet size usually doubles in the final betting round.

strategy.basic: In Lowball, do not stay in the hand after the first draw unless you are drawing to a 7ndlow or better (e.g., holding A-2-3).
strategy.intermediate: The 'Second Draw' trap: Many players overndcommit to a hand that failed to improve on the first draw. Be willing to fold on the second betting round if you still haven't paired your low cards.
strategy.advanced: Bluffing the 'Stand Pat': Standing pat on the first draw even with a mediocre hand can force opponents to fold, as it signals you already have a completed, powerful low hand.
tips: Avoid pairing up. A pair of 2s is worse than a Kingndhigh with no pairs.
In the second draw, only draw one card. Drawing two cards to improve a hand is statistically very risky.
